data.title: The long way home
data.description: A shoreline, a detour, and six seconds of quiet.
data.coverAlt: An illustrated coastline in muted green, sand, and terracotta.

entries.body:
I left the house with a plan to get somewhere. By the water, the plan felt less interesting than the way there.

The tide had drawn a new line across the sand. Someone had left a very small stack of stones. Beyond the bend, the path disappeared into the trees.

## A walk in three frames

```ssb-media-spotlight
![A rust-coloured sun hangs above a green shoreline.](/media/sample-shore.png)
[A slow drift along the illustrated shoreline](/media/sample-shore-film.mp4 "video")
![A winding path crosses layers of green hills.](/media/sample-hills.png)
```

The film is six seconds long and silent. That is about how long I stood still before deciding to keep walking.

> Some days, the detour is the part you came for.

## What came back with me

Not much: a sentence, an idea for a drawing, and the sense that the afternoon had become a little larger.

I put the pictures in [Daylight](/daylight/). If you want an excuse for your own detour, take the [field guide](/field-guide/).

*Sample story and original illustrations. No real journey is being documented.*

data.title: A desk with room
data.description: An open notebook, one useful question, and a little less clutter.

entries.body:
I cleared the desk until only three things remained: a notebook, a pencil, and a cup. The cup was mostly an excuse to sit down.

![An open notebook, pencil, and coffee on a warm wooden desk.](/media/sample-desk.png)

The empty space did not make the work easier. It made the next thing easier to see.

## One useful question

Before starting, I wrote: **What would make today feel complete?** Not impressive. Complete.

| Keep | Put aside |
| --- | --- |
| One small task | A list of twenty |
| A rough first pass | The perfect opening |
| A ten-minute window | Waiting for a free day |

By lunch there was a paragraph on the page. It was not the paragraph I expected, which was a good sign.

## A quiet minute

[A slow shoreline study, six seconds without sound](/media/sample-shore-film.mp4 "video")

This tiny film sits in the middle of the story because words sometimes need an interval.

- [x] Clear a little space.
- [x] Write the first sentence.
- [ ] Come back tomorrow.

If a blank document feels too formal, try the [writing room](/writing-room/). Ten minutes is plenty for a beginning.

data.title: Four studies in light
data.description: The same small palette, four different afternoons.

entries.body:
These drawings began as a rule: four colours, a few shapes, and no detail that did not earn its place.

```ssb-media-grid
![Warm light falls across a tall arched window.](/media/sample-window.png)
![A notebook and coffee sit in a diagonal band of sunlight.](/media/sample-desk.png)
![A terracotta sun glows above the shoreline.](/media/sample-shore.png)
![A light path runs between dark green hills.](/media/sample-hills.png)
```

The window feels still. The desk feels expectant. The shore seems to be leaving. The path seems to be arriving.

## What changed

The palette stayed nearly the same. The amount of empty space did not. Leaving more room around a shape made it feel less like an object and more like a place.

You can switch the collection to **Spotlight** to spend a moment with each drawing. The same images live in the [gallery](/gallery/?tag=daylight).

*Original sample illustrations, drawn for this site.*

data.title: An afternoon at the movies
data.description: A little space for someone else’s imagination.

entries.body:
A personal journal can have a screening room, too. This one has a single seat and no programme to keep up with.

[Big Buck Bunny — Blender Foundation short film](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ "video")

The player loads only when you choose to play it. The film stays with its original publisher.

## After the credits

Write down one image you remember. Not a review, not a verdict. Just an image.

Mine would go beside the drawings in [Daylight](/daylight/), or in the [writing room](/writing-room/) while it is still fresh.

*Film credit: [Blender Foundation / Big Buck Bunny](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ). Linked here as a sample external video.*

data.title: A place to begin
data.description: Sample entry: on making a small space for ideas, without needing to know where they lead.

entries.body:
*This is sample content. Edit it in the browser editor, unpublish it, or remove its Markdown file from the repository.*

There is something useful about a blank page. It asks very little: a thought, a sentence, perhaps an observation from the walk home.

This journal is a place to collect those things. Not everything needs to become a project. Sometimes it is enough to notice, and to write it down.

## Making a little room

The internet can feel like a place where everything has to be finished. A personal site offers a different possibility. You can leave a question open. You can return to an idea months later.

> Start with what you noticed. The rest can follow.

For now, the plan is simple:

- Write when there is something worth remembering.
- Keep the pages comfortable to read.
- Let the collection grow at its own pace.

If you are curious about the person behind these notes, there is an [about page](/about/).

data.title: The value of small things
data.description: Sample entry: a notebook, an afternoon walk, and the quiet satisfaction of paying attention.

entries.body:
*This is sample content, included to show how a second journal entry looks.*

Some of the most useful things I own are also the simplest. A notebook that fits in a pocket. A mug with a comfortable handle. A list of books I might read one day.

Their value is in how often I return to them.

## A small experiment

For a week, I tried writing down one thing each day that I would otherwise forget. Nothing dramatic: the light on a wall, a good sentence, the name of a tree.

By Sunday I had seven small reasons to pay more attention.

The point was not to turn the habit into a system. It was to make a little more of the day visible.

entries.body:
This is sample content inside **Stupid Simple Blogging**. The original journal entries and About page are still here.

## Take a look around

| Try | Where |
| --- | --- |
| A standalone homepage | [Home](/) |
| Posts, tags, and older pages | [Journal](/blog/) and [Topics](/tags/) |
| Images and video in one collection | [The long way home](/blog/the-long-way-home/) |
| Grid and Spotlight | [Daylight](/daylight/) |
| Inline images, video, and formatting | [A desk with room](/blog/a-desk-with-room/) |
| Filtered images and films | [Gallery](/gallery/) |
| Columns and inline HTML snippets | [Layout studio](/layout-studio/) |
| An interactive HTML page | [Writing room](/writing-room/) |
| A multipage PDF | [Field guide](/field-guide/) |
| Search across posts and pages | [Search](/search/) |

The **Explore** menu has nested groups. The footer combines text, links, an image, icons, and an HTML note. The header stays visible while you read.

## Make it yours

Open the editor at the site's usual admin address. **Content** holds these posts and pages. **Media** holds their pictures and films. **Design** holds the small homepage, post, and site-wide additions. **Settings** holds the homepage choice, menu, footer, logo, and text.

All of these examples can be edited or removed through those controls. Nothing needs to be published to GitHub just to try an edit locally.

## Credits

The drawings, silent shoreline clip, writing-room tool, and printable field guide were made for this sample. They can be reused with the site. The sample stories are fictional.

[Big Buck Bunny](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aqz-KE-bpKQ) is linked from the Blender Foundation's video. It is an external embed, not a bundled film.

data.title: A small field guide
data.description: Three printable pages for a slower afternoon.
data.reading:
## Page 1 — A small field guide

Stupid Simple Blogging · Sample edition

Three pages for a slower afternoon. No destination required.

![An illustrated shoreline: green waves and a sandy coast beneath a warm orange sun.](/media/sample-shore.png)

Take a short walk. Notice one thing you would usually pass. Bring back a sentence, a shape, or a question.

Print it, keep it on your phone, or leave it open beside a notebook.

A little room for noticing.

## Page 2 — Leave the route a little open

Out there.

Fifteen minutes is enough. So is the view from a window.

1. **Look for a line.** The edge of a shadow. A branch against the sky. A path that bends out of sight.
2. **Wait for a change.** Stay with the view for a minute. What moves? What stays? What did you miss at first?
3. **Keep one detail.** Write a sentence. Draw a shape. Record a few quiet seconds. One thing is enough.

> There is no right thing to come back with.

Leave places as you found them. The smallest observation can make a good story.

## Page 3 — Keep a little of it

Back here.

The printable page leaves blank space for a date, a place, and these four prompts. You can also answer them in your own notebook or text editor:

- One thing I noticed
- A colour, sound, or shape
- The sentence I want to keep
- Something to return to

An original sample booklet for Stupid Simple Blogging. Made to be printed, scribbled on, and changed.

Until the next small detour.

entries.body:
*A sample now page · October 2026*

## Making

A set of simple illustrations. A journal that feels lived in. Enough room for both words and pictures.

## Noticing

The light arrives at the desk a little later each morning. The notebook still opens to yesterday's page.

![Coffee and a notebook in the afternoon sun.](/media/sample-desk.png)

## Trying

- One short walk without headphones.
- Ten minutes in the [writing room](/writing-room/).
- Printing the [field guide](/field-guide/) and leaving it by the door.

## Leaving open

What should this place become? For now, a useful answer is: somewhere to return to.

data.title: A small place for good things.
data.description: Field notes, little experiments, and things worth keeping.

entries.body:
![An illustrated green shoreline, a warm sun, and a winding band of sand.](/media/sample-shore.png)

Welcome in. This is a sample corner of the internet: a journal to read, pictures to linger over, and a few things to try.

## Start somewhere

- **[Take the long way home](/blog/the-long-way-home/)** — a walk told in pictures and a short film.
- **[Look at the light](/daylight/)** — a small collection, with room to browse.
- **[Make ten minutes](/writing-room/)** — an uncluttered place to write.
- **[Keep a field guide](/field-guide/)** — three printable pages for your next slow afternoon.

## Three things, lately

A window at four. A notebook left open. The line where water meets land.

```ssb-media-grid
![Afternoon light across an arched window and a potted plant.](/media/sample-window.png)
![An open notebook and a cup of coffee on a sunlit desk.](/media/sample-desk.png)
![A pale footpath winds through overlapping green hills.](/media/sample-hills.png)
```

## Come back when you like

The [journal](/blog/) holds the longer stories. [Topics](/tags/) connect the loose threads. The [gallery](/gallery/) gathers the pictures and films in one place.

No hurry. There is always another page.
